source.title: Fight for Washington State: Can Artificial Intelligence Beat the Asian Giant Hornet?

source_quality.summary: All 25 pages were read and visually reconciled. The source contains yearly stochastic propagation, a logistic shape check, mixed-format cleaning and a comment-length null, imbalance repair, autoencoder and three classifiers, geographic priority, derivative update timing, Bayesian eradication proxies, sensitivity, conclusion, code and a team infographic.

decisions: where and how rapidly to inspect, which images deserve positive probability, which region to process first, when to retrain both models, what monitoring signal can trigger further eradication review, and how the public should submit evidence

title: Fight for Washington State: Can Artificial Intelligence Beat the Asian Giant Hornet?
unresolved_questions: The source PDF is a paper response, not the official problem statement.
The European 49.5 km/year rate does not directly identify Washington spread.
The cited $113.7 million scenario is not this paper's forecast.
Initial positive sightings are not guaranteed to equal nest locations.
Three spatial groups do not prove exactly three initial nests.
Latitude/longitude accuracy is assumed rather than audited.
WSDA photo labels are assumed error-free in the assumptions but later classifier error is acknowledged.
Detection date is assumed equal to photo date.
Photo outcomes are assumed independent.
Nearby random foraging is asserted without movement data.
Water is the only forbidden habitat class in the terrain mask.
All land cells receive identical suitability.
Hyperparameters calibrated locally are promoted statewide without a transfer test.
Annual steps omit within-year reproduction, movement and control.
Gaussian competition scale is not empirically calibrated.
Environmental friendliness uses a binary terrain simplification.
Poisson fertility imposes mean-equals-variance dispersion.
The 35% queen fertilization value is not propagated as uncertainty.
Exponential nearby migration omits human-mediated long jumps.
The simulation lacks a documented random seed and repeat distribution.
Eleven-year simulation output is not observed future data.
Logistic fitting to the simulation is internal plausibility, not external validation.
The reported logistic loss 0.076 has no scale-normalized benchmark.
The fastest-growth year 2027 depends on the simulated path and fitted curve.
Manual extraction from video, Word and PDF can introduce selection error.
The 4,426-to-2,127 cleaning transition lacks a row-level ledger.
Comment-length ANOVA tests length, not semantic value.
F significance 0.072 only fails to reject at the selected 5% level.
Dropping all comments overgeneralizes the narrow length test.
Positive-class counts differ across raw, supplemented, flipped and training descriptions and require audit.
Downloaded positive images may differ from citizen-submission distribution.
Image flipping does not create new backgrounds, scales or viewpoints.
Ordinary SMOTE's failure is argued but not experimentally compared.
Borderline-SMOTE on encoded/image features can create unrealistic samples.
The cited 1:4 ratio is not a universal optimal class balance.
Train/test partitioning occurs after several manual and augmentation decisions.
The test set is repeatedly used for checkpoint and hyperparameter selection.
Auto-encoder reconstruction loss does not measure hornet-identification information.
The minimum test loss at iteration 1605 is subject to test leakage.
Binary logistic accuracy 0.5303 lacks class-sensitive metrics.
SVM gamma is selected on the same test set used for reporting 0.5758.
CNN checkpoint selection uses maximum test accuracy at 490 iterations.
Accuracy 0.8030 can hide false negatives under imbalance.
No precision, recall, specificity, calibration or confusion matrix is reported.
Six displayed CNN predictions are not a representative validation sample.
The ten highest negative-probability cases are correct negatives, not error cases.
Negative-feature taxonomy does not explain CNN internals.
Small insects and soft backgrounds may increase both false negatives and true negatives.
CNN probability calibration is not demonstrated before priority aggregation.
Sixty-three pending/unverified records form a small spatial sample.
Single-link clustering is sensitive to chaining and outliers.
Euclidean distance on latitude/longitude requires geographic scale care.
Silhouette favors two clusters, but the operational override uses an asserted patrol diameter.
The five-cluster choice lacks staffing, road-network and travel-time constraints.
At-least-one probability assumes independent image outcomes.
Regional priority rises with the number of reports even at equal per-image risk.
Table/prose cluster references include a possible identifier inconsistency.
Seattle-center interpretation depends on the current pending-report sample.
Age-threshold training sets are nested and not independent experiments.
Stochastic retraining repeats and confidence bands are absent.
Cubic-spline interpolation can move derivative extrema between tested thresholds.
The central-difference truncation statement does not quantify total modeling error.
Four and three months are rounded from 119.39 and 85.71 days.

The page 25 team infographic reverses the body result by assigning three months to the auto-encoder and four months to the CNN; the page 18 experiment and its derivative values support auto-encoder four months and CNN three months, so the conflict must remain explicit rather than being silently harmonized for agency use.
Growth, range and positive-report ratios all depend on reporting effort.
Multiplying the three ratios is not ecologically calibrated.
The Bayesian correction lacks a complete likelihood/prior specification.
K approaching zero cannot prove biological eradication under imperfect detection.
Sensitivity explanations are plausible but do not isolate causal mechanisms.
The infographic's public and staffing recommendations require field, accessibility, cost and safety validation.

Seattle-center interpretation depends on the current pending-report sample.
Age-threshold training sets are nested and not independent experiments.
Stochastic retraining repeats and confidence bands are absent.
Cubic-spline interpolation can move derivative extrema between tested thresholds.
The central-difference truncation statement does not quantify total modeling error.
Four and three months are rounded from 119.39 and 85.71 days.

The page 25 team infographic reverses the body result by assigning three months to the auto-encoder and four months to the CNN; the page 18 experiment and its derivative values support auto-encoder four months and CNN three months, so the conflict must remain explicit rather than being silently harmonized for agency use.
Growth, range and positive-report ratios all depend on reporting effort.
Multiplying the three ratios is not ecologically calibrated.
The Bayesian correction lacks a complete likelihood/prior specification.
K approaching zero cannot prove biological eradication under imperfect detection.
Sensitivity explanations are plausible but do not isolate causal mechanisms.
The infographic's public and staffing recommendations require field, accessibility, cost and safety validation.
